construction_notes: Each Likert response is scored 1-5, with 5 the most motivated response; 'do not know/do not want to answer' is imputed with that year's sample mean (1.33% of responses for financial motivation, 0.46% for patient-oriented altruism).
Item scores are summed within each source of motivation (four items for financial motivation, three for patient-oriented altruism) and then min-max standardised to a 0-1 scale.
GP-level scores are averaged across GPs working in the same practice to give a practice-level motivation score.
A confirmatory factor analysis supports the two-factor measurement model and its invariance over time (Appendix B).
Observations are weighted by the share of GPs in the practice who responded to the work life survey that year.
Quality indicators are measured over the first 6 months of each year 2020-2023; motivation over the second half of each year 2019-2022 (a 6-month lag).
Polypharmacy is defined as more than 5 concurrent prescriptions.
NSAID quality is the average DDDs of NSAIDs prescribed WITHOUT an accompanying proton-pump inhibitor.
For prescribing indicators lower values reflect higher quality; for remunerated-service indicators higher values reflect higher quality.
Patients' health status is proxied by the Charlson Comorbidity Index built from hospital diagnoses in the past 5 years recorded in LPR.
Time-varying covariates and motivation are entered as deviations from their practice-specific means, with the practice means entered separately (within-between / Mundlak parameterisation).

claims.statement: Within practices over time, a higher lagged practice-average level of financial motivation is not statistically significantly associated with the average number of prescriptions issued to enlisted patients over 65.

definition.value: Practice-average GP financial motivation, measured as the extrinsic-motivation sum score over four validated items of the Danish national GP work life survey (5-step Likert, min-max standardised to a 0-1 scale), averaged across the responding GPs of the practice, lagged to the second half of year t-1, and entered as the deviation from the practice's own average over 2019-2022, i.e. (M_it-1 - M-bar_i). Its coefficient beta_w is the within estimate.

timing.value: measured in the second half of year t-1 (2019, 2020, 2021 or 2022), i.e. a 6-month lag before the quality indicator, which is measured in the first half of year t

definition.value: Practice-level average number of prescriptions issued to enlisted patients over 65 years old, computed from the Danish National Prescription Register (LMDB), which contains patient-level data on all prescriptions redeemed in community pharmacies; measured over the first 6 months of each year 2020-2023. Lower values reflect higher quality of care.

timing.value: first 6 months of year t (2020, 2021, 2022 or 2023)

units.value: prescriptions per enlisted patient over 65, per one-unit (0-1 scale) increase in practice-average lagged motivation

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices in the study sample; the authors explicitly decline a causal interpretation, so the quantity is a conditional association between year-to-year changes in a practice's own average motivation and year-to-year changes in its quality indicator
estimand.time_horizon: quality indicator measured over the first 6 months of year t; motivation measured in the second half of year t-1, i.e. a 6-month lag

population.description: Unbalanced panel of Danish general practices that were open (as classified by the Danish Provider Register) and active (as indicated by their patient list size) throughout the study period and whose GP(s) responded to the national GP work life survey at least once between 2019 and 2022; 3286 practice-year observations from 1248 general practices (755 in 2020, 842 in 2021, 841 in 2022, 848 in 2023).
population.period: quality indicators: first half of 2020-2023; motivation: second half of 2019-2022; study period 2019-2023
population.selection: practices open and active throughout the study period with at least one GP responding to the Danish national GP work life survey; these practices account for 46.3%-54.1% of all general practices in Denmark

identification.source_of_variation: Year-to-year changes in a practice's own average lagged motivation score around its practice-specific mean (the practice-demeaned term M_it-1 - M-bar_i) in a within-between (Mundlak/hybrid) random-effects panel model. There is no exogenous shock or reform; the authors explicitly decline a causal reading.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional mean independence: conditional on the included patient, practice and area characteristics and time dummies (and, for the within estimate, the practice averages that absorb time-constant practice heterogeneity), the motivation measure is mean-independent of the error term. The paper states this is what a causal reading would require.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the authors state the requirement and immediately say they cannot verify it: they include a rich set of controls, report entropy-balanced and unadjusted specifications (Appendices Q-T), but decline a causal interpretation

claims.statement: Within practices over time, a higher lagged practice-average level of patient-oriented altruism is not statistically significantly associated with the share of enlisted COPD and asthma patients 18 years and up who receive a spirometry test.

definition.value: Practice-average GP patient-oriented altruism, measured as the patient-orientation sum score over three validated items of the Danish national GP work life survey (5-step Likert, min-max standardised to a 0-1 scale), averaged across the responding GPs of the practice, lagged to the second half of year t-1, and entered as the deviation from the practice's own average over 2019-2022, i.e. (M_it-1 - M-bar_i). Patient orientation captures a non-paternalistic altruism focused on maximising patients' utility. Its coefficient beta_w is the within estimate.

timing.value: measured in the second half of year t-1 (2019, 2020, 2021 or 2022), i.e. a 6-month lag before the quality indicator, which is measured in the first half of year t

register_source.value: SSR (Danish National Health Insurance Service Register) + LPR (Danish National Patient Register)

definition.value: Practice-level share of enlisted COPD and asthma patients 18 years and up who receive a spirometry test; because the test can be delivered in general practice or in hospital, the Danish National Health Insurance Service Register (SSR) is combined with hospital records in the Danish National Patient Register (LPR); measured over the first 6 months of each year 2020-2023. Higher values reflect higher quality of care.

timing.value: first 6 months of year t (2020, 2021, 2022 or 2023)

units.value: share of enlisted COPD and asthma patients (0-1), per one-unit (0-1 scale) increase in practice-average lagged motivation

claims.statement: Across practices, a higher practice-average level of lagged patient-oriented altruism is not statistically significantly associated with the share of enlisted patients over 75 years old receiving a preventive home visit.

definition.value: Practice i's average level of patient-oriented altruism (patient-orientation sum score, min-max standardised to 0-1, averaged across responding GPs) across the entire motivation measurement period 2019-2022, i.e. M-bar_i. definition.value: Practice-level share of enlisted patients over 75 years old receiving a preventive home visit, computed from the Danish National Health Insurance Service Register (SSR), which covers publicly funded primary care services; measured over the first 6 months of each year 2020-2023. identification.source_of_variation: Differences in practice-average lagged motivation across general practices (the term M-bar_i) in a within-between (Mundlak/hybrid) random-effects panel model, conditional on observed patient, practice and area characteristics. ambiguities: The authors explicitly decline a causal interpretation of every estimate in Table 1 ('we are careful not to interpret any of the estimates as causal relationships'). The identification strategy recorded here describes the estimator actually used (the within/between decomposition of a Mundlak random-effects panel model), not a causal claim the paper makes.

Table 1 attaches a single star to this coefficient, which the table note defines as p < 0.10. statistically_significant is recorded as false because the paper's own text uses a 5% threshold and, for the sleeping-medication between estimate, states explicitly that 'the coefficient estimate is statistically insignificant in the main model specification'; the results section also enumerates the significant patient-oriented-altruism between estimates and does not include the home-visit indicator. The printed p-value bound (p < 0.10) is recorded as given.

The baseline mean is printed as a rounded percentage in the text ('around 5%', 'around 14%', 'approximately 11%' etc. for the first half of 2020) and was divided by 100 to put it on the 0-1 share scale of the regression outcome; the exact figure is in Supporting Information S1: Appendix C, which is not part of this PDF.

Both sources of motivation enter the same regression simultaneously, each with a within and a between term, so the coefficient recorded here is conditional on the other motivation as well as on the listed controls.

evidence.how: The paper reports the baseline practice-level mean of this indicator as a percentage; the regression outcome is a share on a 0-1 scale (the text reports effects such as 'an increase of 0.006 in the share'), so the printed percentage was divided by 100.
